Hi all,

Attaching the calc workbook (LD-4721_runway_calc_v2.xlsx). Key technical assumptions and outputs below so procurement has context without opening the sheet:

Assumptions
- Model family in baseline: 13B dense (quantized to 4-bit QAT profile) for UI; 70B variant available as fallback for high-quality reports but kept behind a higher-cost tier.
- Avg tokens per response (median): 420 tokens; worst-case tail 1,200 tokens (10% of requests).
- Average generation speed per GPU (approx):
  * 13B Q4x4: 260–320 tps per GPU (batching 8–16, FP16 emulation + kernel tuning).
  * 70B Q4_K_M: 45–60 tps per GPU (larger context, KV management overhead).
- Typical request life cycle: prefix + gen. We account for KV reuse for conversational flows (~25% reduction in effective tokens/sec for returning users).

Derivation (peak):
- Peak concurrent requests (UI + web spikes): 40 concurrent.
- Weighted avg tokens per request at peak: 480 (mixing med + some long tails).
- If average response generation latency target is 1.0s for compute (network + orchestration separate), tokens/sec required = concurrency * tokens_per_request / compute_seconds = 40 * 480 / 1.0 = 19,200 tps.

Mapping to GPUs
- Using conservative per-GPU tps of 270 for 13B profile (to account for message routing and jitter): 19,200 / 270 ≈ 71.1 GPU-equivalents. That number is high because tps is per-GPU-second; dedicated pools operate with multi-request batching — we convert to worker counts via expected throughput per worker over 1s windows.
- Practical mapping (production packaging + autoscale/burst): we recommend starting with 8 physical GPUs in a dedicated pool, with each GPU running multiple worker replicas (containerized runtime) distributed across the pool. The 8-GPU recommendation is based on Redwood's serving model that aggregates concurrency into fewer, highly-utilized workers with continuous batching and KV cache warmness. This gives expected 1.4x headroom for bursty spikes; it is often more cost-effective than naively converting tps -> GPU count.

SLA fit and caveats
- With 8 GPUs and Redwood's routing (traffic-symmetric placement + warm KV), simulated 95th latency at your token distribution falls between 380–500ms depending on tail ratio. To keep 95th < 450ms consistently, we recommend either:
  a) 8 GPUs + tighter batching latency cap + 10% concurrency cap, or
  b) 10 GPUs for a simpler margin at higher commit cost.

If procurement is risk-averse, option (b) is easiest to defend. Option (a) requires more operational tuning but saves committed capacity and cost.

I've included a tab with per-token cost at 3 commit levels (8, 10, 12 GPUs) and an amortized monthly $/1M tokens number. Marcus — see the notes on the 70B fallback economics.

Laura
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Priya / Arun — quick follow-up after our internal review. Summary + recommended contract language to keep SLAs feasible while minimizing committed spend:

1) Recommended commit: 8 Dedicated GPUs with an optional ramp to 10 within 90 days if 95th latency exceeds 450ms for two consecutive weeks. We can add an auto-burst policy to the Dedicated pool for short-term spikes (3x nominal for up to 10m per hour).

Example SLA clause (suggested):
"Redwood will maintain a Dedicated pool sized at 8 GPUs for the contracted environment. If observed production 95th-percentile latency for interactive UI workloads exceeds 450ms for more than two consecutive weeks, Redwood will either: (i) provision an interim burst increase to 10 GPUs within 72 hours at no additional one-time provisioning charge, or (ii) provide a credit to LambdaMed consistent with the service-level credit schedule attached."

2) Final items we need from procurement to finalize pricing:
- Confirmation of peak concurrent users expected during business hours (you supplied 40; please confirm if that includes API partners).
- Any regulatory requirement forcing on-prem or VPC-only hosting (affects baseline infra cost).
- Confirmation whether 70B outputs will be allowed as part of the pilot (higher per-token cost).

3) Deliverables we attached: LD-4721_runway_calc_v2.xlsx (detailed math), SLA-proposal-LambdaMed.pdf (wording + credit table).

If that looks fine, Jonas — let's mark this ready for procurement and I'll spin up a short one-page slide for exec sign-off.

Thanks,
